Hech qachon. Faqat Player ID va platforma yetarli. Sizdan parol, SMS kodi yoki akkauntga kirish so'ralsa, bu firibgarlik — darhol to'xtating va @StarsPaymeeSupport ga xabar bering.

faq.q: Gameloft ID ni ulash nega muhim?
faq.a: Chunki u progressingiz va tokenlaringizni akkauntga bog'laydi, qurilmaga emas. Telefon yo'qolsa yoki ilovani o'chirsangiz, ID orqali hammasini tiklaysiz. Ulanmagan mehmon akkauntida esa hamma narsa o'sha qurilmada qolib ketadi.

collisions.problem: The single worst duplicate on the site. Same publisher (Moonton), same currency word (olmos), same ID format 123456789(1234), same discovery path (tap avatar top-left), near-identical answerBox, near-identical slug, both carrying HowTo schema for the same procedure. They will compete head-on for the un-branded blockers 'server id qayerda turadi', 'zone id nima', 'user id va server id farqi' — the exact queries both plans name as their highest-intent target. Google will pick one and suppress the other, and it will probably pick the wrong one.
collisions.fix: MLBB owns the generic mechanic: keep its H1/answerBox as-is, add 'Zone ID' and 'server raqami' as explicit synonyms, keep the HowTo schema. Reposition MCGG entirely onto the confusion query it uniquely owns — rename H1 to 'Magic Chess: Go Go ID si Mobile Legends ID si bilan bir xilmi?', slug to magic-chess-go-go-id-mobile-legends-farqi, primaryKeyword to 'magic chess go go mobile legends id farqi', lead with the answer (separate app, separate ID, one Moonton account), cut the find-the-ID steps to 3 lines + link to the MLBB page, and drop HowTo schema from it. Add reciprocal 'bu boshqa o'yin' links between the two.

collisions.problem: Seven comparison pages built from one template with ~80% shared body: 'official store wants Visa, foreign resellers price in USD, Telegram sellers are risky, GemPay takes UzCard/HUMO in so'm'. Game-qualified queries won't cannibalise, but the un-qualified head terms ('o'yin puli qayerdan arzon', 'donat qayerdan olish arzon', 'uzcard bilan donat') have seven equal claimants and no canonical page — so none of them ranks. Worse, seven near-duplicate pages published in one quarter is a textbook templated-doorway pattern.
collisions.fix: Build the hub two of these plans already link to (oyin-valyutasi-qayerdan-arzon) and let it own the un-qualified head terms and the shared payment-rail argument. Then cut each game page down to one genuinely game-specific decision axis and delete the boilerplate: PUBG = Midasbuy; MCGG = Codashop + region SKU (Rossiya/Global/Turkiya); Free Fire = region lock + crypto/gift-card; CODM = Garena vs Global build; MLBB = in-game Google Play billing; Asphalt = platform routing; HOK = Midasbuy/Level Infinite. Each keeps a max 60-word rail summary linking up to the hub.

collisions.problem: A real head-to-head, not a template one. Both target Midasbuy as their central axis: PUBG's secondaries include 'midasbuy uzcard qabul qiladimi', 'midasbuy o'zbekiston to'lov', 'midasbuy узбекистан оплата картой'; HOK carries 'honor of kings midasbuy uzbekistan' plus a full FAQ 'Midasbuy O'zbekistonda ishlaydimi?'. The generic query 'midasbuy o'zbekiston / midasbuy uzcard' — which the PUBG research flags as high-volume failure-intent traffic — has two claimants on the same domain.
collisions.fix: PUBG owns Midasbuy outright: give it the verdict section, the FAQ, and the payment-matrix table, and consider a dedicated spin-off page 'Midasbuy O'zbekistonda ishlaydimi' for the failure-intent traffic. HOK reduces to one sentence ('Midasbuy — rasmiy kanal, lekin O'zbekiston kartalari odatda qo'llab-quvvatlanmaydi') with a link out, and pivots its axis to Level Infinite Pass / official-vs-reseller instead.

collisions.problem: 'Bepul olmos / bepul token / bepul CP generator' scam content is written seven times: once as a standalone page (Free Fire) and six times as a full H2 or warning block elsewhere. Because three of these games all call the currency 'olmos', the generic query 'bepul olmos generatori ishlaydimi' is split three ways before you even count the token/CP variants. The Free Fire plan correctly identifies this as the largest-volume cluster in its vertical — and then lets six other pages dilute it.
collisions.fix: Free Fire keeps the standalone page as site-canonical, but brand-lock the title/H1/answerBox to 'Free Fire bepul olmos' so it never fights on the bare term. Every other mention drops to a 40-60 word warning + link, with no H2 of its own (fold it into the existing checklist or warning block). If you want the bare 'bepul o'yin valyutasi' term, it belongs on the oyin-pul-xavfsiz-toldirish hub, not on a game page.

collisions.problem: Systemic across all seven clusters, shown here with PUBG: the pillar, the info page and the comparison page each carry a full price-logic block saying the same thing (provider price → USDT rate → so'm moves daily → exact figure is in the bot). That's 21 near-identical sections site-wide. The pillar and info page additionally both publish the full pack ladder (60/325/660/1800/3850/8100), so 'pubg uc paketlari' and 'pubg uc narxi' each have two claimants inside one cluster.
collisions.fix: One price-logic block per game, on the info page only — it is the page whose search intent is 'how does this work'. The pillar gets a single sentence plus the live figure from the bot; the comparison page gets a comparison-methodology paragraph ('bir birlikka to'g'ri keladigan so'mni solishtiring') which is a different claim, not the same one. Pack ladder lives on the info page as a table; the pillar shows it as a bare inline list with no commentary.

collisions.problem: Three pages carry the same Settings → User Settings → Player ID steps, and both the pillar and garena-global-farqi list 'call of duty mobile player id qayerda' / 'garena player id topish' as target keywords. Separately, the CODM cluster is the only one of the seven with no trust-type article — garena-global-farqi is typed 'howto' and is doing double duty as ID guide, version explainer and safety page, while codm-cp-kelmadi duplicates its wrong-version diagnosis.
collisions.fix: Make garena-global-farqi the canonical ID + version page: promote 'call of duty mobile player id qayerda' to a primary keyword, retype it 'trust', keep the HowTo schema. Pillar drops to two sentences + link and removes those keywords. The problem page keeps only the symptom-level 'ID topilmadi' triage and links out for the explanation. Note that CODM still has no free-CP-scam / account-safety page — that content currently sits orphaned inside cod-points-cp-nima.

collisions.problem: Free Fire is the only cluster with no dedicated UID page, yet its own research lists 'free fire uid qayerda' and 'free fire player id topish' as target queries and Google-suggest confirms 'honor of kings player id'-class demand for this pattern. The UID content is split between the pillar (a 4-step H2) and the problem page (which literally puts 'id-topilmadi' in the slug and spends a section on six causes). Two half-answers, no page that can rank for the blocker query, and the problem page's slug promises an answer its own H1 frames as post-payment triage.
collisions.fix: Split the problem page: keep free-fire-olmos-kelmadi-nima-qilish for post-payment triage (region lock, delivery delay, MAX shared balance, bonus diamonds), and create free-fire-uid-qayerda as the trust/blocker page owning UID discovery, UID-vs-nickname, guest-account linking and 'UID berish xavfsizmi'. This restores the 5-type pattern the other six clusters follow and captures pre-purchase traffic the cluster currently forfeits.

collisions.problem: Broken and phantom internal links pointing equity at 404s. MCGG links to 'mobile-legends-olmos-toldirish' (the real slug is mobile-legends-olmos-sotib-olish) from two pages, plus 'pubg-uc-payme-click', 'pubg-uc-yetkazish-vaqti', 'oyin-valyutasi-qayerdan-arzon', 'oyin-pul-xavfsiz-toldirish' and 'gempay-ishonli-xizmat' — none of which exist in the supplied set. HOK references the same three hubs but with a /blog/ prefix while MCGG uses bare slugs, so even if they are built the URLs disagree.
collisions.fix: Fix the MLBB slug typo. Decide one path convention (recommend bare slug rendered as /blog/<slug> for articles, /oyinlar/<game> for money pages) and enforce it in the template rather than per-plan. Then either build the three hubs before publishing anything that links to them, or strip those links. Also fix the misspelling: 'gempay-ishonli-xizmat' should be 'gempay-ishonchli-xizmat'.

collisions.problem: All 35 articles carry FAQPage schema, and three questions repeat near-verbatim across roughly 15 pages each: 'akkaunt parolim kerakmi', 'qancha vaqtda keladi', 'narx nega o'zgaradi'. That is the same Q/A pair marked up 15 times on one domain — it dilutes AEO extraction (the model has no reason to prefer any one page) and invites Google to ignore the markup site-wide. Compounding it, the delivery promise is inconsistent between pages of the same brand: ~1 min (MLBB), ~2 min (PUBG, MCGG, FF), ~3 min (CODM, HOK), ~5 min (Asphalt), with escalation thresholds of 15 min, 30 min, and 'sezilarli vaqt'.
collisions.fix: Keep the shared trio in FAQPage schema on the pillar of each cluster only; on spokes keep them as on-page text outside the schema block, or reword to a genuinely page-specific angle. Standardise the delivery language: one site-wide sentence ('o'yinga qarab odatda 1-5 daqiqa') plus the per-game figure, and one escalation threshold everywhere (15 daqiqa) so support policy and content agree.

collisions.problem: Not keyword cannibalisation — budget cannibalisation, which costs more. Ten of 35 articles (29% of the programme) go to two games with, by their own research, near-zero measurable Uzbek demand: HOK's plan reports empty Yandex/Google suggest for every Uzbek HOK prefix and the game is still pre-launch in UZ; Asphalt's plan reports the Uzbek SERP returns road-construction results because 'asfalt' means road asphalt. Meanwhile Telegram Premium/Stars — the brand's own home turf, same audience, same wallet, and the pattern the Asphalt and CODM research explicitly names as the proven winner (uzgets.uz, starsjoy.uz) — gets zero articles.
collisions.fix: Cut HOK to 3 (pillar, player-id, comparison) and Asphalt to 2 (pillar, player-id/platform — the platform-vs-server explainer is genuinely the most defensible page in the whole set, uncovered in any language). Redeploy the 5 freed slots to the Telegram Stars/Premium cluster and the three missing hubs. Revisit HOK at full depth when UZ launch traffic actually appears in Search Console.

synthesis.verdict:
START HERE: the payload contains 7 plans and 35 articles, not 9 and 45. Two plans are missing, and the evidence says they were the site-level layer — four articles link to 'oyin-valyutasi-qayerdan-arzon', 'oyin-pul-xavfsiz-toldirish' and 'gempay-ishonli-xizmat', none of which exists in any plan supplied. Everything below covers the 35 I actually received; my ordering and graph reserve slots for those three hubs because the rest of the site is already built assuming they exist.

The individual plans are strong — the keyword research is honest about what was verified versus inferred, and the no-invented-prices discipline is right. As one site they have a different problem: this is seven copies of one template, and nobody audited the seams. Four things will actively cost money.

1. Duplication is the real risk, not competition. The Uzbek SERP is genuinely empty for six of seven games, so ranking is easy; what will hurt is publishing 35 pages where the same six blocks (price logic, 'parol so'ralmaydi', 'qancha vaqtda keladi', free-currency scams, wrong-ID-is-non-refundable, payment-rail table) repeat 7-21 times each. Price-logic alone appears 21 times. The differentiation work in the collisions list is not polish — it is the entire job between this plan and a doorway-page penalty.

2. One true cannibalisation pair: the MLBB and MCGG ID pages. Same publisher, same currency word, same ID format, same discovery path, near-identical slugs and answer boxes, both with HowTo schema. Fix that one before writing a word.

3. The budget is allocated backwards. Ten of 35 articles (29%) go to Honor of Kings and Asphalt 9 — two games whose own research reports empty autocomplete, a pre-launch status, and an Uzbek SERP collision with road asphalt. Zero articles go to Telegram Premium/Stars, which is the brand's own product, the same audience, the same wallet, and the pattern three of these very plans cite as the proven winner. Cut HOK to 3 and Asphalt to 2, and move those five slots to Stars/Premium and the three hubs. (Keep asphalt-9-player-id-qayerda regardless — the platform-vs-server explainer is uncovered in any language and is the single most defensible page in the whole set.)

4. Every plan verified real Russian demand and not one produced a Russian URL. In Uzbekistan that is the larger half of transactional search on Yandex, sitting in keyword lists with nowhere to land. Ship /ru/ mirrors with hreflang for at least the top 10 pages, or drop the Russian keywords from the briefs so writers stop stuffing them into Uzbek body copy.

Publish order rationale: MLBB and PUBG pillars first (largest demand, weakest incumbents — PUBG's only real competitor is a ~200-word Payme blog post), then ID/blocker pages, which are pre-purchase blockers with zero competition and the highest conversion assist per word. Comparison pages next (decision stage, captures failed-Midasbuy and failed-Codashop checkout traffic). Problem pages after that — highest intent but the searcher has already paid, so they earn retention and support deflection, not first purchase. Info pages last in every cluster. Publish each cluster's pillar in the same sprint as its spokes so internal links resolve on first crawl.

Three hygiene items to fix in the template, not per article: the broken link to 'mobile-legends-olmos-toldirish' (real slug is -sotib-olish, wrong in two MCGG articles) plus three other phantom targets; inconsistent path convention (bare slug vs /blog/ prefix vs /oyinlar/); and the delivery-time promise, which varies between 1 and 5 minutes with escalation thresholds of 15 min, 30 min and 'sezilarli vaqt' across pages of the same brand. Also standardise slugs — 'magic-chess-go-go-olmos-kelmadi' drops the -nima-qilish suffix its six siblings carry, and '-paketlar' vs '-paketlari' vs '-qayerdan-arzon' vs '-qayerdan-arzon-olish' vary for no reason.

Finally, cap FAQPage schema for the three universal questions to the cluster pillar only. Repeating identical Q/A markup 15 times gives no page a reason to be the cited one — which defeats the AEO play these plans are otherwise well built for.
